cleanIntro: The subcompact of the VP line: 6.61 inches overall on a 3.39 inch barrel, 24.3 oz with an empty magazine, and a shortened accessory rail with three slots instead of the full-size gun's four. It strips with no tools like every VP, but almost nothing else about its hardware is interchangeable with the full-size — the Long Slide kit does not fit it, and its magazines are a family of their own.

steps.title: Point it safe, magazine out, slide locked back
steps.action: Muzzle safe and finger outside the trigger guard. Depress either side of the ambidextrous magazine release and pull the magazine out of the well, then grasp the rear serrations, rack the slide fully to the rear and lock it there on either slide release. Watch the ejection port for a cartridge or case leaving.
steps.prose: On a subcompact the rear serrations are short and the slide is stiff. Get a full grip on them rather than pinching the back of the slide.
steps.quote: 2. Remove the magazine. Depress either side of the ambidextrous magazine release. Remove the magazine from the magazine well. 3. Open and lock the slide to the rear. Grasping the rear serrations, rack the slide to the rear while keeping the muzzle pointed in a safe direction. Push upwards on either side of the ambidextrous slide release and lock the slide to the rear.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 4 — CLEARING PROCEDURES, p.11
steps.warn: The firearm is not empty or unloaded until the magazine is removed and the chamber is clear.

steps.title: Chamber check by eye and by finger
steps.action: With the slide locked back, look into the chamber through the ejection port and then sweep the chamber and feed ramp with a finger. Remove anything found. The VP9SK's port is physically smaller than the full-size gun's, which makes the visual check less conclusive and the finger sweep more important.
steps.prose: Cold hands and a short port are how a chambered round gets missed on a carry-size pistol.
steps.aside: The three sub-steps printed under it are: visually inspecting the chamber through the open ejection port; physically inserting a finger through the ejection port and sweeping the chamber and feed ramp area; and removing any cartridges or empty cases.
steps.quote: 4. Inspect the chamber. Inspect the chamber for the presence of a cartridge or empty case by:
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 4 — CLEARING PROCEDURES, p.11

steps.title: Know which VP9SK magazine you have out
steps.action: Before the pistol goes on the bench, account for the magazine you removed. The VP9SK takes an unusually wide range: flat-floorplate and hooked-floorplate 10-round magazines, and extended 13, 15 and 17 round magazines with sleeves. HK also notes the standard full-size VP9 15-round magazine fits the VP9SK.
steps.prose: That cross-fit is worth knowing during a strip, because a full-size magazine standing on the bench next to a subcompact is otherwise easy to mistake for the gun's own.
steps.quote: ACCESSORY MAGAZINES FOR VP9SK A variety of magazines and accessory floorplates are available for different operational requirements and for optimal ergonomic handling; these include a flat floorplate magazine (10 round capacity), a hooked floorplate magazine (10 round capacity), and extended magazines (13, 15, and 17 round capacity) with extended floorplates/magazine sleeves.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 7 — ACCESSORY MAGAZINES FOR VP9SK, p.40

steps.title: The disassembly safety gates the whole strip
steps.action: The lever will not turn until the pistol is in the right state. A magazine in the well — loaded or empty — pivots the disassembly safety up and blocks the lever, and a forward slide blocks it too. Magazine out and slide locked back is the only condition in which it moves.
steps.prose: Do not lever it. A disassembly lever that will not rotate is reporting the pistol's condition, and forcing it is how the safety gets broken instead of obeyed.
steps.caution: If it will not turn, something is still in the gun.
steps.quote: The disassembly safety ensures that the magazine must be removed from the magazine well, the chamber be cleared, and the firing pin decocked prior to disassembly. The disassembly safety is pivoted upwards by the presence of a magazine (loaded or unloaded) and thus blocks the operation of the disassembly lever.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 3 — Safety Features, p.10

steps.title: Disassembly lever down to six o'clock
steps.action: With the slide locked back and the magazine out, rotate the disassembly lever on the LEFT side of the frame down until it points to roughly six o'clock. Take it fully round — a partial rotation leaves the slide captured and the frame is short enough that there is little leverage to spare.
steps.prose: The lever on the SK sits in the same place as on the full-size gun but with less frame around it, so a fingernail is often better than a thumb.
steps.quote: 2. With the slide still locked to the rear and the magazine removed, rotate disassembly lever, located on the left-hand side of the frame, downward until the lever is pointing to approximately the six o'clock position (see Figure 18).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — DISASSEMBLY, p.20

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Depress the slide release and push the slide FORWARD off the top of the frame. It leaves over the muzzle end, not the rear. On the SK the slide is short and light, so it comes away faster than you expect.
steps.prose: Cup a hand over the front as it goes. Subcompact slides have less mass and land harder for it.
steps.quote: 3. Depress the slide release and push the slide forward, removing the slide from the top of the frame (see Figure 19).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — DISASSEMBLY, p.20

steps.title: Recoil spring forward, then out to a side
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down and push the recoil spring FORWARD, then out to the left or the right, freeing it from the barrel and slide. The SK's spring is short and stiff — it stores as much energy in less travel, so it comes out with more urgency than the full-size unit.
steps.prose: Two hands and a bench. The rear of the guide rod is what disengages and it is a small part to chase.
steps.quote: 4. Turn the slide upside down and carefully push the recoil spring forward and out to either the left or right side, separating the recoil spring from the barrel and slide (see Figure 20).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — DISASSEMBLY, p.20

steps.title: Barrel out through the ejection port
steps.action: Pivot the barrel slightly forward and press UP on the barrel locking block through the ejection port. That is the lug beneath the chamber that engages the port cut; lifting it clears the block and the 3.39 inch barrel lifts out.
steps.prose: On a short barrel there is very little to grip, so press the block rather than trying to pull the barrel.
steps.quote: 5. Pivot the barrel slightly forward and press upward on the barrel locking block through the ejection port, separating the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — DISASSEMBLY, p.21

steps.title: ⛔ Bronze bore brush only — the bore is polygonal
steps.action: Clean the 3.39 inch bore with a BRONZE bristle brush in the correct calibre, six passes chamber to muzzle, then patches. HK bars steel brushes outright because they scratch the polygonal rifling and cost accuracy — and on a short barrel there is less bore to give any accuracy back.
steps.prose: This is the one cleaning rule in the book that comes from how HK cuts its barrels rather than from general practice.
steps.quote: CAUTION: Do not use a steel bore brush which can scratch the polygonal bore and reduce accuracy.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.26
steps.warn: No steel brushes in a polygonal bore.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Slide, barrel, recoil spring and frame. HK's specification table for the VP9SK says the same as the full-size gun's: no tools for the user field strip, and simple punches for a detailed depot-level strip that is not owner work. Note the SK's own rail is the reduced-length MIL-STD-1913 with three slots — a full-size light or laser mount will not necessarily index on it.
steps.prose: That three-slot rail is on the SK's specification page, not the full-size gun's, and it is one of the details a shared-book manual makes easy to read off the wrong table.
steps.quote: Reduced length MIL-STD-1913 rail with three slots located under dust cover
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 2 — Specifications (VP9SK/VP9SK-B SUBCOMPACT), p.8

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The Long Slide kit does NOT fit a VP9SK
deepSteps.action: Before you buy or fit anything, know this limit. HK's VP Long Slide accessory kit — extended slide, extended barrel and its own recoil spring assembly — is stated to fit any standard-size VP frame, and stated NOT to fit the subcompact models. Your VP9SK is one of those.
deepSteps.prose: It is the clearest model boundary in this shared manual, and it is the reason the SK cannot simply be treated as a short VP9.
deepSteps.quote: The Long Slide components do not fit the subcompact models of the VP series.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 7 — VP LONG SLIDE, p.37
deepSteps.warn: Subcompact frames are excluded from the Long Slide kit.

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Paddle or push button is fixed at purchase
deepSteps.action: The VP9SK exists with either the ambidextrous paddle release or a reversible push button — HK's Figure 39 shows the push-button SK specifically. The two are model specific and CANNOT be converted in either direction; only the push button itself can be moved from left to right with a punch or a pen.
deepSteps.prose: So a magazine-release problem on this pistol is a parts question, not a configuration question.
deepSteps.quote: CAUTION: The paddle magazine release and the reversible push button are model specific. An HK VP handgun with a paddle magazine release cannot be converted to a push button magazine release. The push button magazine release model cannot be converted to a paddle magazine release. This determination must be made at time of purchase, as the two models are not convertible.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 7 — PUSH BUTTON MAGAZINE RELEASE, p.33

deepSteps.title: Magazine floorplate off — punch, hand over the base, slide forward
deepSteps.action: On a high-capacity VP9SK magazine, depress the locking plate in the floorplate with a punch and hold it. Put a hand over the base to control the spring, then slide the floorplate FORWARD off the housing and let the locking plate and spring expand out gradually.
deepSteps.prose: The SK's extended 13, 15 and 17 round magazines carry sleeves over the body — take the sleeve into account before assuming the floorplate is where you think it is.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Using a punch, depress the locking plate located in the floorplate and hold it there (see Figure 25). 2. Place a portion of either hand over the base of the magazine to control the release of the magazine spring and locking plate. 3. Slowly slide the floorplate forward off the mag­az­ ine housing (see Figure 26).
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY, p.23
deepSteps.warn: WARNING: Always keep the base of the mag­az­ ine point­ed in a safe direction (away from the face and eyes).

deepSteps.title: 10-round magazines come apart differently
deepSteps.action: A 10-round VP magazine does not use the same floorplate catch. Depress the locking INSERT in the floorplate with a punch, hold it, put a hand over the base, and while the insert is still depressed squeeze the floorplate locking TABS on the right and left sides of the magazine. Then let the insert and spring out gradually.
deepSteps.prose: The SK ships with 10-round flat and hooked floorplate magazines as standard options, so this is the procedure most VP9SK owners will actually use.
deepSteps.caution: Locking INSERT plus side TABS — not the high-capacity procedure.
deepSteps.quote: Disassembly of 10-round magazines: 1. Using a punch, depress the locking insert located in the floorplate and hold it there (see Figure 29).
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY, p.23

deepSteps.title: Normal cleaning across all five groups
deepSteps.action: Nylon toothbrush and solvent over the slide's internal surfaces, then rag and swabs. Bronze bore brush six passes chamber to muzzle, patches, then the toothbrush over the barrel exterior and locking block. Recoil spring assembly with solvent and a brush. Frame concentrating on the area normally under the slide. Magazine follower and feed lips.
deepSteps.prose: On a carry pistol the frame area under the slide collects lint as well as carbon, and lint is what stops a subcompact slide short.
deepSteps.quote: • Moisten a bronze bore brush with solv­ ent and scrub the bore from chamber to muzz­ le at least six (6) pass­es, back and forth.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — Normal Cleaning, p.26

deepSteps.title: Major cleaning after 500 rounds or contamination
deepSteps.action: After 500 cartridges, or exposure to sand, dust, water — salt water especially — or other visible contaminants, HK escalates: the magazine is disassembled and every part rinsed or immersed in solvent, scrubbed with a nylon brush, then dried with compressed air or a rag and swabs before reassembly and lubrication.
deepSteps.prose: HK warns that ultrasonic cleaning can remove the coloured reference markings from the frame, extractor and control lever, and says it is not normally necessary below 10,000 rounds.
deepSteps.caution: Everything must be thoroughly dried after immersion, then lubricated.
deepSteps.quote: Major Cleaning - Major Cleaning is the same as normal cleaning ex­cept that: • The magazine is dis­as­semb­ led for cleaning. • All parts should be rinsed with or immersed in solv­ ent and thoroughly scrubbed with a nylon brush.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — Major Cleaning, p.27

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Alter nothing
deepSteps.action: HK ends the inspection section with a prohibition that covers everything you have just had apart: do not alter any part of the pistol or magazine, including attempts to improve it. Doing so may cause serious injury or death, damage the pistol, and voids the warranty.
deepSteps.prose: On a subcompact carry gun the temptation is to smooth or lighten something. This is the manufacturer saying the answer is a different part, not a modified one.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING: Do not alter any of the parts or components of the pistol or magazine, e.g., do not attempt to “improve” or make the pistol “better” by altering parts or components.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — INSPECTION, p.27

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Nylon toothbrush moistened with solvent over all internal surfaces
Rag and cotton swabs to lift the loose fouling
Check the breech face and the extractor claw

cleaning.name: BARREL (3.39 in) AND LOCKING BLOCK
tasks: Bronze bore brush, six passes chamber to muzzle — never steel on a polygonal bore
Scrub the barrel exterior and locking block with the nylon toothbrush

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING AND FRAME
tasks: Solvent and a nylon brush over the recoil spring assembly
Scrub the frame where carbon shows, concentrating on the area normally covered by the slide
Clear lint from the rails and the three-slot accessory rail

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Scrub the follower and feed lips of every magazine, flat, hooked and extended
High-capacity magazines use a locking PLATE; 10-round magazines use a locking INSERT plus side tabs
Check each follower slides freely and rises nearly flush against the feed lips
Remember the full-size VP9 15-round magazine also fits this pistol

cleaning.name: INTERVALS
tasks: Normal cleaning after each firing or every twelve months, whichever comes first
Major cleaning after 500 cartridges or after sand, dust, water or other contaminants
Store clean, lubricated and with the slide forward

reassembly: Turn the slide upside down and insert the barrel with its angular locking surface facing upwards, then pivot it rearward until the locking block snaps into the ejection port.
Insert the pronged end of the recoil spring into the tang on the slide above the muzzle.
Push the spring forward, compressing it, then pivot the rear of the guide rod onto the stepped mounting surface on the front of the barrel locking lug, front of the spring facing forward.
With no magazine in the well and the disassembly lever still down, mount the slide on the frame with the spring centred under the barrel and the frame rails in the slide grooves.
Pull the slide back — pressing down on the rear of the slide if the rear frame insert does not engage — and lock it back on either slide release.
Pivot the disassembly lever counterclockwise until it lies horizontal to the bottom of the slide.
fncheck: Clear the VP9SK, then rack the slide three or four times in quick succession and confirm it runs freely with no binding. Return it forward, and with the pistol empty and pointed safely pull the trigger for an audible click. Rack and release while holding the trigger back, then release the trigger and listen for the reset click that signifies the firing pin is engaged by the sear. Insert an empty magazine and rack: the slide must lock back — check this with a 10-round flat floorplate magazine AND with any extended magazine you carry, because the followers differ.
